heading: AI & Compute Intelligence
subheading: The capex supercycle, silicon stack, foundation-model giants & the bubble debate
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. AI is the market's most crowded trade; concentration and drawdown risk are significant. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: Amazon (~$200B), Alphabet ($195–205B), Microsoft (~$175B CY2026 guide / ~$255–260B FY2027 all-in), Meta ($130–145B) and Oracle (~$70B FY27) — combined $775–800B, ~75% AI-specific and roughly 3x the ~$238B spent in 2024. Debt funding has grown from 9% of capex in FY24 to 32% over the trailing twelve months (FactSet); Alphabet priced an $84.75B equity raise in June and Oracle plans $40B of debt+equity for FY27

Up from $47B annualized in May; Q2 preliminary revenue topped $11.5B with the company's first-ever operating profit (Axios/Bloomberg, Aug 17). Backers reportedly target $100–120B annualized revenue by year-end and an October IPO at $2T or more — which would eclipse SpaceX's $1.77T IPO valuation as the largest listing ever

Global venture funding per Crunchbase, already topping all of 2025's $440B; AI captured ~70–80% of it. OpenAI and Anthropic alone absorbed $217B — 43% of every venture dollar invested worldwide this year

bear_case.title: The revenue gap
bear_case.description: The AI industry is burning an estimated $400B+ a year in infrastructure spend against $50–60B of direct AI revenue generated — a gap that keeps widening as hyperscaler capex guidance keeps rising, with the top-5 hyperscaler total now pegged at $775–800B for 2026. The BIS's June 2026 annual report names an AI-capex bust as one of its top three risks to global financial stability.

bear_case.title: Rates are now the transmission mechanism
bear_case.description: A late-July chip selloff has given way to a rate-driven one: the 30-year Treasury hit 5.32% on Aug 18, the semiconductor index (SOXX) fell nearly 5% in a single session, and CoreWeave — one of the most debt-heavy AI infrastructure names — dropped 12%. NVIDIA (-2.34%) and AMD (-4.27%) fell too despite no company-specific bad news, evidence a debt-funded buildout is now directly exposed to financing-cost risk, not just AI-demand risk.

bear_case.title: Off-balance-sheet obligations turning concrete
bear_case.description: Moody's flags ~$662B of signed-but-not-commenced data-center lease commitments sitting off hyperscaler balance sheets, and debt funding of the buildout has risen from 9% of capex in FY24 to 32% over the trailing twelve months (FactSet). NVIDIA's own Aug 10 response — $500B of financing MOUs with Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to move AI infrastructure onto institutional balance sheets — shows how much outside capital the next leg of the buildout now requires. Oracle remains the starkest case: ~$70B of FY2027 capex funded by a fresh $40B of debt and equity, a BBB- downgrade, and an FY26 cash outflow that already ran $23.7B ahead of what the company generated.

bear_case.title: Circular financing
bear_case.description: Interlocking vendor-equity stakes and take-or-pay compute deals among NVIDIA, Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic, Oracle and CoreWeave — echoing the Lucent/Nortel vendor-financing dynamics of 1999–2001 — make end-demand look larger and more independent than it is. Analysts peg the web of circular deals at over $800B; CNBC's Jim Cramer has repeatedly compared the pattern to the dot-com bubble, and the BIS flags a "circular financing collapse" as a top-three global financial-stability risk.

bear_case.title: Depreciation clock
bear_case.description: Hyperscalers depreciate AI hardware over 5–6 years, but bears argue the chips' real economic life is closer to 2–3 years — an estimated ~$176B understatement of depreciation across 2026–2028 that flatters reported earnings, with Oracle's earnings overstated by an estimated 26.9% and Meta's by 20.8% by 2028 on this analysis. Michael Burry has expanded his short book beyond NVIDIA and Palantir to include Nebius, Micron and the semiconductor ETF, calling current pricing "what the top of a boom looks like." Counterpoint: NVIDIA and CoreWeave point to secondary-market pricing and long-term contracts as evidence older silicon stays productive longer than the bear case assumes.

bear_case.title: Layoffs while capex soars
bear_case.description: Oracle cut ~21,000 jobs and is now guiding to ~$70B of FY2027 capex funded substantially by new debt, even as Microsoft cut another ~4,800 in July. Tech-sector layoffs are running at a 20-year high. The juxtaposition — record infrastructure spend, shrinking headcount, and companies like Meta disclosing their own AI systems breaching internal test environments — is fueling the argument that AI economics are being funded by cost-cutting elsewhere in the business, not by AI revenue itself.

bear_case.title: Concentration everywhere
bear_case.description: AI is simultaneously the market's largest index weight, VC's largest allocation (OpenAI and Anthropic alone took 43% of a record $510B global H1 2026 venture total), and this hub's connective thread — a drawdown would hit robotics, nuclear, storage and quantum sentiment at once, as the Aug 18 rate-driven selloff already demonstrated across chip names. Counterpoint: infrastructure vendors keep posting record quarters (TSMC's 2nm demand already exceeding 3nm, Broadcom's reiterated $100B+ FY2027 AI semiconductor guide) — some strategists call the bear case premature given actual demand signals.

positions.name: NVIDIA
positions.note: Data Center revenue still $75.2B in Q1 FY27 (+92% YoY), and NVIDIA signed $500B in AI-infrastructure financing MOUs with Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR (Aug 10) — a sign the buildout increasingly needs outside institutional capital, not just hyperscaler cash. Aug 26 earnings (guided $91B±2%, Street modeling $91.85–95B) is the next real test, coming right after an Aug 18 rate-driven chip selloff. Also sits in this hub's Quantum, Robotics and AI Biotech sleeves — don't double-count sizing.

positions.name: TSMC
positions.note: Q2 revenue $40.2B (+34%) still stands, and fresh reporting shows 3nm output rising ~20% by year-end while 2nm demand already exceeds 3nm — evidence the runway extends well past this cycle. Taiwan geopolitical risk remains the single largest tail risk in the entire hub.

positions.name: Alphabet
positions.note: Still the only genuinely full-stack position — TPUs, Gemini, Waymo (cleared for full CA expansion). Alphabet raised its capex guide to $195–205B and priced an $84.75B equity raise in June to help fund it — a reminder that even the strongest balance sheet in the group is now tapping outside capital. Also appears in the Quantum sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: Microsoft
positions.note: Azure's $80B unfulfilled order backlog (power-constrained, not demand-constrained) remains the standout bull signal. Guided capex looks lower at ~$175B for CY2026, but that's a lease-accounting reclassification, not a real cut — FY2027 all-in spend is still estimated near $255–260B. Also in the Quantum sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: Amazon
positions.note: AWS's 37% growth (fastest in 18 quarters) and Q2 revenue crossing $200B for the first time hasn't been challenged by anything new this week. Still the cheapest way to own AI demand inside a business that already prints cash.

positions.name: Broadcom
positions.note: Reiterated FY2027 AI semiconductor revenue guidance above $100B with visibility to 2028, and CEO Hock Tan called XPU/networking demand "simply insatiable." The Aug 14 stock slide (-5.9%) traced to an unrelated VMware security scare, not the AI business — noise, not signal.

positions.name: Palantir
positions.note: No incremental print since last week's eighth straight quarterly beat and raised FY26 guide to $8.16B; conviction unchanged, still sized modestly given the multiple assumes near-flawless execution.

positions.name: AMD

positions.name: Meta
positions.note: CFO Susan Li describing 2026 capital planning as "highly dynamic" is corporate-speak for "we don't have a capex ceiling yet" — reinforcing the same capex-to-AI-revenue gap and governance concerns (sandboxed model breach) that kept this a Watch last week.

positions.name: UiPath
positions.note: Nothing this week changes the core problem: being disrupted by the agent wave it markets itself as part of.

positions.name: Oracle
positions.note: Now guiding ~$70B of FY2027 capex funded by a fresh $40B of combined debt and equity — the backlog story keeps getting more expensive to sustain, layering onto the existing BBB- downgrade, Wisconsin collateral demand, and FY26 cash burn.

positions.name: SpaceX
positions.note: Mixed evidence this week: xAI capex more than doubled to $15.8B in Q2 (2x Q1, above the $13.09B Street estimate), but Alphabet agreed to pay SpaceX $920M/month from Oct 2026–Jun 2029 for ~110,000 Nvidia GPUs — real recurring revenue. Not enough clarity yet to move off Watch.
